done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: The amount guard still requires at least one linking token after an amount word. Consequently, a clear amount phrase such as `Show actual amount 2025` does not match `LINKED_AMOUNT_YEAR_PATTERN`: the final `amount` has no following link, so `calendarYear` accepts 2025 and replaces the model/prior window with calendar year 2025. On a follow-up this returns the wrong period instead of inheriting the prior window. This is new evidence distinct from the ruled `Actual to/of 2025` cases and the now-covered `totalling to 2025` case.
findings.title: Not done: an amount is never read as a year

findings.body: The added matrix and rerun tests exercise `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose LLM, executor/warehouse, audit, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes. The frontend period-control tests also mock the API. The registered suite at `package.json:26` and `backend/package.json:18` contains no Playwright/browser path through a running API and real database. Therefore named-period precedence, no-period inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and changing the answer period still lack the required user-flow proof. The successful close run only confirms these mocked service/jsdom boundaries, so the prior test-audit blocker remains open.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
